key_insight: Adding an EHR-integrated radiologist dashboard did not make STAT chest X-ray reports more specific overall, but it modestly improved diagnostic concordance and lowered follow-up chest CT use.
clinical_relevance: This suggests better contextual data at the point of interpretation may improve downstream care decisions even when it does not change reporting language much.
method: Stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial across 15 service areas in an integrated health system.
Included 404,860 ED and inpatient STAT priority chest radiographs read by 387 radiologists.
Used LLM-based report classification with expert validation to assess specificity, concordance, and downstream utilization.
evidence_signal: Large-scale trial data showed no change in report specificity, but a statistically significant rise in abnormal report–discharge diagnosis concordance and a small reduction in follow-up chest CTs.
watch_item: The dashboard’s benefits were modest and depended on LLM-based outcome classification, so real-world implementation may require careful validation and workflow fit.
paper_title: Effect of an Electronic Health Record-Integrated Clinical Dashboard for Radiologists on STAT Priority Chest Radiograph Reporting and Downstream Care: A Stepped-Wedge Cluster Randomized Trial
